purpose: Reason about content and task fit before selecting an arrangement. Entries are hypotheses, not mandatory templates.

shared: Choose by intended outcome, content relationships, cardinality, evidence and action consequence.
Keep section surfaces full container width; inner content may use an intentional max-width and automatic inline margins for centered layout or readable prose.
A named pattern is an initial hypothesis. Adapt or invent a better arrangement when the content warrants it.
Prefer the best supported fit for this task; no template is universally objectively best without context and evaluation.
marketingWebsites: Compose a sequence of audience decisions, not a sequence of interchangeable feature cards.
Use purposeful variety in density, representation and emphasis to mark changes in meaning and reduce monotonous scanning.
Inspect adjacent and page-wide repetition: semantic duplication, identical silhouette, repeated cognitive demand and repeated conversion asks.
Break a pattern where the narrative changes: recognition to mechanism, mechanism to evidence, evidence to fit, fit to commitment.
Preserve a coherent visual grammar. Novelty that adds decoding effort without advancing understanding is not valuable variety.
A repeated pattern can aid comparison or orientation. Do not enforce a fixed diversity quota or prohibit all repetition.
Place a conversion hook when the visitor has gained new grounds for acting; vary commitment appropriately, not merely button wording.
contentWebsites: Vary discovery and topic-orientation surfaces by reader intent; preserve predictable reading and reference structures within a content type.
An editorial pause must clarify the argument rather than interrupt comprehension.
productExperiences: Optimize for correctness, learnability, repeat-use efficiency and recovery. Stable object/action placement usually outweighs novelty.
Use consistent templates for equivalent objects and tasks; change structure when content relationships or consequences differ.
Queues suit actionable sets, detail suits one object, matrices suit comparable options, workbenches suit creation. Evaluate the fit rather than rotate them for variety.
dashboardsAndAgents: Keep metrics and state semantics stable across views. Vary structure for a different decision, not decorative refresh.
Distinguish evidence, inference, recommendation, authority, action and outcome. Progressive detail should preserve traceability.

patterns.title: Problem contrast
patterns.intent: Recognize the gap between a current situation and a useful change.
patterns.selectWhen: The audience recognizes the situation but not the value of changing it.
patterns.avoidWhen: The two states cannot be compared fairly.
patterns.tradeoff: Contrast can overstate the product’s effect.
patterns.evaluation: Can a visitor describe the difference without inferring an unsupported outcome?

patterns.title: Process sequence
patterns.intent: Explain order, prerequisites and the next responsibility.
patterns.selectWhen: Sequence is the cause of understanding or successful completion.
patterns.avoidWhen: Steps are actually independent features or a branching network.
patterns.tradeoff: A linear depiction can hide loops and dependencies.
patterns.evaluation: Can someone identify the next step and what blocks it?

patterns.title: Dependency map
patterns.intent: Make relationships and blockers legible.
patterns.selectWhen: The useful explanation concerns what depends on what.
patterns.avoidWhen: The task is simply to scan unrelated benefits.
patterns.tradeoff: A map can become difficult to read as relationships grow.
patterns.evaluation: Can the reader trace one dependency and explain its consequence?

patterns.title: Inspectable specimen
patterns.intent: Show the actual shape of a result or working object.
patterns.contentShape: One credible object with representative fields
patterns.selectWhen: Evaluators need to understand what they would receive or work with.
patterns.avoidWhen: No truthful sample exists, or a decorative screenshot would stand in for evidence.
patterns.tradeoff: A single specimen can appear more representative than it is.
patterns.evaluation: Can a reviewer explain what the object shows and what it does not prove?

patterns.title: Role or need routes
patterns.intent: Help people find a relevant path without reading everything.
patterns.selectWhen: Different visitors need materially different explanations or actions.
patterns.avoidWhen: Audience categories overlap so much that the route choice is arbitrary.
patterns.tradeoff: Asks the visitor to self-identify before learning more.
patterns.evaluation: Can a visitor choose a route and recover from a wrong choice?

patterns.title: Evidence narrative
patterns.intent: Let a reader assess a result in its original context.
patterns.selectWhen: Credibility and transferability are central to the decision.
patterns.avoidWhen: There is no source or the content is only an invented endorsement.
patterns.tradeoff: A vivid example may be overgeneralized.
patterns.evaluation: Can the reader distinguish observation from inference and assess applicability?

patterns.title: Comparison matrix
patterns.intent: Compare alternatives on shared dimensions.
patterns.selectWhen: A decision depends on cross-option comparison with consistent definitions.
patterns.avoidWhen: Dimensions are incomparable or the table would mostly contain marketing adjectives.
patterns.tradeoff: Wide matrices are costly on narrow screens.
patterns.evaluation: Can someone explain a tradeoff across two alternatives using the same criterion?

patterns.title: Fit and limitation band
patterns.intent: Help the right audience recognize fit and others recognize non-fit.
patterns.selectWhen: A limitation materially affects whether the next step is appropriate.
patterns.avoidWhen: It merely repeats legal boilerplate without a decision consequence.
patterns.tradeoff: Over-compression can hide nuance.
patterns.evaluation: Can a poor-fit visitor identify an appropriate exit?

patterns.title: Question and answer disclosure
patterns.intent: Resolve specific residual uncertainty without burying the main narrative.
patterns.selectWhen: Secondary questions differ between readers and can be progressively disclosed.
patterns.avoidWhen: The answer is essential to consent, price or understanding the main claim.
patterns.tradeoff: Collapsed answers may never be read.
patterns.evaluation: Can the reader find the uncertainty that changes their decision?

patterns.title: Bounded next-step invitation
patterns.intent: Connect accumulated understanding to an appropriate commitment.
patterns.contentShape: Action, expected outcome, required effort and alternative
patterns.selectWhen: The page has established enough context for a useful next action.
patterns.avoidWhen: It interrupts before relevance is established or adds pressure without new value.
patterns.tradeoff: Repeated asks can create fatigue or pressure.
patterns.evaluation: Can a visitor explain the commitment and choose to defer?

patterns.title: Editorial interlude
patterns.intent: Give one consequential idea room to register.
patterns.selectWhen: A narrative shift benefits from reduced density and a clear connection.
patterns.avoidWhen: It is filler, an unsupported slogan or a fake quote.
patterns.tradeoff: A pause spends scroll length and can become theatrical.
patterns.evaluation: Does the next section gain clarity from the pause?

patterns.title: Annotated mechanism
patterns.intent: Explain how one capability produces a useful effect.
patterns.contentShape: An object or mechanism with mapped explanations
patterns.selectWhen: The mechanism is easier to understand visually than through feature prose.
patterns.avoidWhen: Annotations merely restate labels or imply functionality that is not demonstrated.
patterns.tradeoff: Too many callouts compete for attention.
patterns.evaluation: Can the reader connect a visible part to the purpose it serves?

patterns.title: Capability index
patterns.intent: Enable scanning and selective depth across peer capabilities.
patterns.selectWhen: Readers know what they seek and need quick coverage.
patterns.avoidWhen: The page needs a causal story or all entries say the same thing.
patterns.tradeoff: Repeated cards flatten priority and can feel monotonous.
patterns.evaluation: Can someone find a relevant capability without opening every item?

patterns.title: Metric with context
patterns.intent: Explain a quantity relative to a meaningful denominator or baseline.
patterns.contentShape: Measure, unit, population, period and comparison
patterns.selectWhen: A supported number helps answer the current question.
patterns.avoidWhen: The number is decorative, unsourced or lacks comparable scope.
patterns.tradeoff: Large numbers can exaggerate certainty.
patterns.evaluation: Can a reader restate exactly what the number measures?

patterns.title: Source register
patterns.intent: Make provenance and limits inspectable.
patterns.selectWhen: Trust or verification requires knowing where information came from.
patterns.avoidWhen: Source quantity is being used as a substitute for source support.
patterns.tradeoff: Deep detail can distract from the main decision.
patterns.evaluation: Can a reader verify a claim and locate counterevidence?

patterns.title: Task queue
patterns.intent: Help a repeat user identify and advance actionable work.
patterns.contentShape: Work items with priority, state and ownership
patterns.selectWhen: Throughput and next responsibility matter more than a broad narrative.
patterns.avoidWhen: Objects need extended comparison or rich editing before action.
patterns.tradeoff: Ranking may conceal work that still matters.
patterns.evaluation: Can a user find the right next task without a wrong-scope action?

patterns.title: Record detail
patterns.intent: Explain an object’s state, history and available actions.
patterns.contentShape: One domain object and its relationships
patterns.selectWhen: The person acts on a known object with consequential state.
patterns.avoidWhen: The task is primarily discovering which object matters.
patterns.tradeoff: Too much metadata can obscure the next action.
patterns.evaluation: Can a user explain the current state and the effect of their action?

patterns.title: Staged form
patterns.intent: Collect dependent input while preserving context and recovery.
patterns.selectWhen: Earlier input changes later questions or a consequential review is needed.
patterns.avoidWhen: A short independent form would be faster and clearer.
patterns.tradeoff: Extra stages add navigation and can hide the total effort.
patterns.evaluation: Can a user correct earlier input without losing valid work?

patterns.title: Contextual workbench
patterns.intent: Let a person create or revise while retaining relevant reference material.
patterns.contentShape: Working artifact, tools and supporting context
patterns.selectWhen: Creation benefits from nearby evidence, preview or critique.
patterns.avoidWhen: The task is one small action that needs little context.
patterns.tradeoff: Dense tools may overwhelm occasional users.
patterns.evaluation: Can the user complete and recover edits while understanding the saved state?

patterns.title: Monitoring brief
patterns.intent: Explain whether a situation warrants investigation.
patterns.selectWhen: A person needs timely orientation before deciding to intervene.
patterns.avoidWhen: There is no defined decision or the user needs open-ended exploration.
patterns.tradeoff: Summaries can encourage premature conclusions.
patterns.evaluation: Can the operator distinguish a true signal from absent or incomparable data?

patterns.title: Scoped approval
patterns.intent: Let a person authorize a specific consequential action.
patterns.selectWhen: Execution exceeds delegated bounds or conditions have changed.
patterns.avoidWhen: Routine permitted work merely adds a meaningless confirmation.
patterns.tradeoff: Too many gates create habituation and rubber-stamping.
patterns.evaluation: Can the reviewer state precisely what is and is not authorized?

patterns.title: Option judgment
patterns.intent: Support choosing among credible strategies with explicit tradeoffs.
patterns.contentShape: Mutually distinguishable alternatives with comparable criteria
patterns.selectWhen: The person owns a value judgment that the system should not silently make.
patterns.avoidWhen: The differences are cosmetic or one option is an obviously invalid decoy.
patterns.tradeoff: Scores may conceal value choices.
patterns.evaluation: Can the user explain why one option fits their intent better?

reasoningGuidance.scope: Marketing and narrative content pages; apply locally within mixed experiences. Product task surfaces retain their own workflow and consistency principles.
use: Use these as revisitable prompts, not a required sequence, questionnaire or scoring rubric. Scale the depth to the decision.
Reason from visitor progress and available means together. Missing evidence can change the story; a strong demonstration can replace several explanations.

Treat spatial footprint, visual emphasis, information density, reading effort, disclosure depth and interaction demand as independent scale decisions. A short statement can carry more narrative weight than a large table.
Choose a module for its contribution and content relationship, then evaluate it in the page sequence. Variety earns its place through comprehension, attention or decision support.
Record concise design conclusions, assumptions and tradeoffs in the brief and relevant intent/rationale fields. Do not require a transcript of private model reasoning or new reviewer form fields.
Evaluate comprehension, qualified progression and confident decisions with explicit definitions and guardrails. Clicks are one signal; prototype preference is not evidence of business impact.

page.prompt: What progress should the visitor make, and what outcome should the organization achieve?
What brings the visitor here? What do they already understand, doubt, need or expect?
What central idea and supporting evidence could move them toward that outcome?
How is that story best experienced: explanation, demonstration, comparison, exploration, testimony or a combination?
What meaningful, digestible parts does the story need? Each part should resolve a question, establish something or enable a decision.
How much attention, detail and space does each part deserve?
What should precede what? Where should the experience accelerate, pause, deepen or change form?
What next action is appropriate at each point, given the visitor’s understanding, confidence and readiness?

module.prompt: What specific job does this module perform within the larger experience?
What must it communicate or demonstrate to perform that job?
Which pattern makes that content easiest to understand, assess or act upon?
What prominence, density, depth and interaction does its role justify?
How does it connect to adjacent modules without unnecessary repetition?
What should the visitor understand, believe or be able to do afterward?

experienceReasoning.purpose: Compose relevant lenses locally. SaaS is a product context, native is a delivery environment, and dashboard is a surface; they are not exclusive project categories.

sharedPrompts.prompt: What progress does the person need to make, and under what operating conditions?
What can the system support, with what constraints, evidence and authority?
What information, decisions and actions connect desired progress to available means?
How should those responsibilities become flows, surfaces and components?
What deserves prominence, detail, density or progressive disclosure?
How will people navigate, interrupt, resume, recover and understand the result?
What observations would demonstrate useful outcomes, and what guardrails prevent misleading success?

lenses.title: Narrative and readiness
lenses.useWhen: A person needs to understand relevance, assess evidence and choose a next step.
questions: What must be understood or trusted before progression?
Where does a change in representation advance meaning or renew attention?
What commitment is justified at this point?
guardrails: Pressure without new grounds for action

lenses.title: Native context and continuity
lenses.useWhen: Device capabilities and interruptible sessions materially shape a task, on mobile or desktop.
questions: What should happen quickly, and what requires sustained attention?
How do permissions, input modality, offline use and device capabilities change the task?
What survives interruption, switching devices or returning later?

lenses.title: Product work and SaaS lifecycle
lenses.useWhen: People create, manage, collaborate on or administer persistent objects.
questions: Which objects, relationships and states organize the work?
How do roles, dependencies, concurrency and repeat use affect completion?
What establishes readiness, supports orientation and separates personal preferences from workspace policy?
guardrails: Speed at the expense of quality

lenses.title: Analysis and intervention
lenses.useWhen: People interpret signals, investigate causes and decide whether to act.
questions: Which question or exception deserves attention?
What baseline, denominator, time range or comparison gives a signal meaning?
How can someone move from overview to evidence, investigation and action?

lenses.title: Delegation and supervision
lenses.useWhen: Agents propose or execute work while people supply objectives, direction, choices or authority.
questions: What may be delegated, under which scope, budget and stop conditions?
When should a person direct, choose, approve or intervene?
What evidence, uncertainty, changes and results make supervision meaningful?

unitPrompts: What responsibility does this unit fulfill within the experience?
What information, evidence and actions are required?
Which representation fits their relationship and consequences?
What prominence, density, depth and interaction does the task justify?
Which entry, working, completion, interruption and recovery states matter?
How does this unit connect to adjacent work and preserve continuity?
What observable result would indicate successful resolution?
experienceReasoning.use: Prompts and measures are candidates, not required fields, fixed sequences or performance claims. Record concise conclusions and consequential uncertainty.
